clue.text: Crustaceans — almost the very same river contained

indicators.note: contained says the river's name sits inside the shortened likeness word
almost means the synonym loses its final letter before use

parts.note: 'the very spit of' someone is their exact likeness, so the very same is SPIT
the Cam is the river through Cambridge

explanation.surface: A diner complains that the prawns came out of the very same river as before.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The very same' is idiom: someone who is the very spit of another looks just like them; 'almost' drops its last letter before the river goes in.
explanation.definitionFit: Scampi are langoustines, small lobster-like shellfish, served breaded.

clue.text: Tightly shut

definitions.meaning: as an adverb, held tightly is held near, pressed snug
a door that is shut has been pulled to

explanation.walkthrough: The two words read as one phrase but each defines the answer separately.
explanation.definitionFit: Hold someone near and snug is hold them so; a door so treated is no longer open.

clue.text: Home at ten, willy-nilly? That's outdated

indicators.note: willy-nilly means haphazardly, so the three words are jumbled into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone who insists on being home by ten is mocked as old-fashioned.
explanation.walkthrough: 'willy-nilly' rearranges the nine letters of HOME AT TEN.
explanation.definitionFit: Clothes eaten by moth larvae are shabby and old, hence the figurative sense of antiquated.

clue.text: At home taking a holiday, somehow

parts.note: someone at home is in
someone on holiday is away

explanation.surface: A puzzle about how one can be at home and on holiday at the same time.
explanation.definitionFit: Saying something is true to some extent or in some sense is a hedge like somehow.

clue.text: Excellent score after mishit at golf

indicators.note: after puts the score word behind the mishit word

parts.note: to top the ball in golf is to hit its upper half, a mishit
to score is to cut a mark, a notch

explanation.surface: A golfer posts a fine score despite a bad shot.
explanation.walkthrough: Topping is a golf mishit where the club strikes the top of the ball.
explanation.definitionFit: First-rate and excellent are synonyms; a top notch is the highest mark.

clue.text: Active Northern boatmen, naturally 'at ease when working

indicators.note: active means busy moving about, so the letters of the next two words are set in motion and rearranged

explanation.surface: Energetic boatmen from the North are naturally comfortable at their work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Active' rearranges the fifteen letters of NORTHERN BOATMEN.
explanation.definitionFit: The Hamlet phrase describes someone who takes to a role or task as if born to it.

clue.text: Chart 'turned up containing a grid that's wrong, for example

indicators.note: containing says the reversed chart word wraps round the jumbled letters
in a down clue, turned up reads the chart word from the bottom, backwards

parts.note: a chart is a map

indicators.note: that's wrong says the letters of a grid are in the wrong order and must be rearranged

explanation.surface: A chart flipped over containing a faulty grid is held up as a model.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'turned up' means read bottom to top; 'that's wrong' jumbles the two words before they are enclosed.
explanation.definitionFit: A paradigm is a model or typical pattern, a standard instance.

clue.text: The Sound of Music lacking a certain energy?

indicators.note: lacking says a letter is missing from the brass band noise

parts.note: taken literally, the sound of (brass band) music is oompah
taken as written

explanation.surface: The famous musical film is accused of lacking some spark.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The Sound of Music' looks like the film title but is read literally as the noise a band makes; 'lacking' removes A from OOMPAH.
explanation.definitionFit: Oomph is vigour or a particular kind of zest, a certain energy.

clue.text: Players I confine to quarters and rebuke severely

parts.note: the players in a show are its cast
to gate a student is to confine them to college as punishment

explanation.surface: A commanding officer confines soldiers to barracks and gives them a dressing-down.
explanation.walkthrough: To gate is British school and university slang for confining a student to the premises.
explanation.definitionFit: To castigate is to reprimand or criticise harshly.

clue.text: He has agreed to direct steering of farm vehicle

parts.note: to con a ship is to direct its steering
a tractor is a farm vehicle

explanation.surface: A farmer agrees to steer the tractor.
explanation.walkthrough: To con (or conn) is the naval term for directing a ship's helmsman.
explanation.definitionFit: A contractor is a person who has signed a contract, agreeing to do work.

clue.text: Make tea in hospital

definitions.meaning: in Britain to ... tea is to brew it
a mobile army surgical hospital is known by its initials

explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is a link between the two definitions; mashing tea is regional British for brewing it.
explanation.definitionFit: Brew tea by steeping it in northern English usage; also the US army field-hospital acronym.

clue.text: Representative from Georgia participating in strike

indicators.note: participating in puts the state abbreviation inside the strike word

parts.note: to strike out text is to delete it
GA is the postal abbreviation for the US state of Georgia

explanation.surface: A representative from Georgia takes part in industrial action.
explanation.definitionFit: A delegate is someone sent to act or vote on behalf of others.

clue.text: Flower trouble had returned

indicators.note: returned means both words are read backwards together, from the end

parts.note: to ail is to trouble

explanation.surface: A gardener says the flower trouble came back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returned' turns AIL HAD into DAH LIA.
explanation.definitionFit: A dahlia is a garden plant with showy blooms.

clue.text: Ammunition is exhausted

definitions.meaning: lead pellets fired from a gun
worn out, tired, in informal British use

explanation.walkthrough: 'is' links the two definitions.
explanation.definitionFit: Lead pellets fired from a gun; informally, also worn out and done for.

clue.text: Cistern is intended to stand up

definitions.meaning: a tank is designed to contain liquid
an argument that stands up is sound and convincing

explanation.walkthrough: The first definition describes the job of a cistern literally.
explanation.definitionFit: Literally a tank's job; figuratively a theory that survives scrutiny.

clue.text: Non-English herb given name relating to Church of England

indicators.note: Non-English says the abbreviation for English is dropped from the herb

parts.note: angelica is an aromatic herb

explanation.surface: A herb is said to have a churchy name.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Non-English' removes E (English) from ANGELICA, leaving ANGLICA.
explanation.definitionFit: Anglican describes the established church of England and its communion.

clue.text: Forbid indirect manoeuvring before time

indicators.note: before puts the rearranged word ahead of the time abbreviation
manoeuvring means moving the letters around into a new order

explanation.surface: An official bans devious tactics ahead of time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'manoeuvring' rearranges INDIRECT into INTERDIC.
explanation.definitionFit: To interdict is to prohibit or ban formally.

clue.text: Middle Eastern money supporting China appears very relevant

indicators.note: in a down clue, supporting puts the money below the china word

parts.note: china is cockney rhyming slang (china plate) for mate, a friend
the rial is the currency of Iran and Oman

explanation.surface: Gulf currency propping up China's economy looks highly significant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'China' looks like the country; in cockney rhyming slang, china plate means mate, a friend.
explanation.definitionFit: Material evidence is evidence that is significant and pertinent.

clue.text: Fruit clearly contains an insect

indicators.note: contains says the insect sits inside the clearly word

parts.note: plain means clear or obvious, as in plain to see
an ant is an insect

explanation.surface: Inspecting a fruit, someone spots a bug inside.
explanation.definitionFit: The plantain is a starchy banana-like fruit eaten cooked.

clue.text: Row producing audible evidence of grief

indicators.note: audible says the word is heard rather than read, giving one with the same sound

parts.note: a tear is a sign of sorrow

explanation.surface: An argument produces audible sobbing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Row' looks like a quarrel; it is a row of seats.
explanation.definitionFit: A tier is a level or rank, a row of seats one above another.

clue.text: Your holding novel up causes complaint

indicators.note: holding says the abbreviation wraps round the reversed title
in a down clue, up means the title reads from the bottom, backwards

parts.note: Emma is the Jane Austen novel

explanation.surface: Holding up your novel provokes grumbling.
explanation.walkthrough: Emma is Jane Austen's novel; in a down entry 'up' means it is written bottom to top.
explanation.definitionFit: Yammer is noisy grumbling or whining.

clue.text: Part of answer verified as "deviation"

indicators.note: Part of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A quiz host confirms that an answer counts as a deviation.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft put 'as' in the definition; 'as' is a link word, so the definition is only 'deviation'.
explanation.definitionFit: A sudden turn off course is a deviation from a line.

clue.text: Grow older in state prison

parts.note: RI is the abbreviation for Rhode Island, a US state
a pen is slang for a penitentiary, a prison

explanation.surface: Someone grows old in a state penitentiary.
explanation.definitionFit: Fruit or cheese that matures with age is said to come to maturity.

clue.text: Policeman reversed into deer, showing aggression when driving

indicators.note: into says the reversed word goes inside the deer word

parts.note: the roe is a small deer

indicators.note: reversed means the policeman word is read backwards

parts.note: a garda is an Irish police officer

explanation.surface: A policeman backs his car into a deer while driving aggressively.
explanation.walkthrough: The Garda is the police force of Ireland, so a single officer is a garda; 'reversed' turns him round before he goes into the deer.
explanation.definitionFit: Road rage is violent anger shown by motorists.

clue.text: Eco-friendly marijuana

definitions.meaning: slang for cannabis, from its colour

explanation.walkthrough: Two separate senses of one colour word.
explanation.definitionFit: The colour word means environmentalist and is also slang for cannabis.

clue.text: Prevent large amount of money being withdrawn

indicators.note: being withdrawn means the money word is pulled back, read backwards

parts.note: pots of money is a large amount

explanation.surface: A bank tries to block a large withdrawal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'being withdrawn' reverses POTS.
explanation.definitionFit: To halt or block something is to prevent it.

clue.text: Cruelly-used girl and I in more trouble

indicators.note: trouble means the letters are disturbed into a new order

explanation.surface: A mistreated girl says she and the speaker are in deeper trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trouble' rearranges AND I IN MORE; the definition is a cryptic description of the torture device, a 'maiden' used cruelly.
explanation.definitionFit: The iron maiden was a spiked cabinet said to be used for torture, a maiden cruelly employed.

clue.text: Benjamin Roosevelt

definitions.meaning: Benjamin's surname, the US founding father
Roosevelt's first name, the US president FDR

explanation.walkthrough: The name is a surname for one and a first name for the other.
explanation.definitionFit: The founding father's surname and the wartime US president's first name are the same.

clue.text: Grandiloquent nonsense — and in German too!

parts.note: rot is nonsense
und is German for and

explanation.surface: A pompous speaker talks rubbish, and in German as well.
explanation.definitionFit: Rotund describes speech that is sonorous and pompous, full-sounding.
